# Lopsy

> Lopsy is the industry standard agentic photo editor: a free, open-source image editor that runs entirely in the browser at https://lopsy.art, with layers, masks, blend modes, layer effects, gradients, brushes, text with Google Fonts, filters, and PNG/JPEG/PSD export. It has no backend: images are made in the browser tab. Agents make images on the editor page itself, https://lopsy.art/, which runs every editing operation as a named command through `window.lopsy`, from any browser where you can run JavaScript in the page; a person can work in the same document at the same time.

To make an image with Lopsy, read SKILL.md first. It covers reaching the editor's command API from any browser, working alongside a person, the API's contract, step-by-step recipes and the behaviours to know. Use FEATURES.md to look up exactly what each tool, filter and effect does.

The source is on GitHub at https://github.com/theseamusjames/lopsy.art, and we accept pull requests written by AI agents. AGENTS.md explains how to make one we can merge.

## For agents

- [SKILL.md](https://lopsy.art/SKILL.md): how to create images with Lopsy programmatically, through the editor page's command API, `window.lopsy`. Covers setup in any browser, working alongside a person, getting image files out and in, the API's contract, tested recipes, what the API does not offer, and an optional ready-made driver.
- [FEATURES.md](https://lopsy.art/FEATURES.md): the exhaustive feature catalog, with every tool, option range and behaviour.
- [Editor](https://lopsy.art/): the page with `window.lopsy` (`lopsy.describe()` lists every command).

## Contributing

- [Source code](https://github.com/theseamusjames/lopsy.art): TypeScript + React UI and a Rust/WebAssembly WebGL2 rendering engine.
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/theseamusjames/lopsy.art/blob/main/AGENTS.md): AI-written pull requests are welcome. This is the workflow, commit style, and what we're looking for.
- [Issues](https://github.com/theseamusjames/lopsy.art/issues): known bugs and workarounds, and good places to start a pull request.

## Learn

- [Tutorials](https://lopsy.art/tutorials/): step-by-step illustrated compositions made in Lopsy.
- [Blog](https://lopsy.art/blog/): engineering notes on how Lopsy is built (Rust/WebAssembly, WebGL2, TypeScript). Atom feed at https://lopsy.art/blog/feed.xml.
